title: Hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state (adult)
subject: endocrinology
summary: Restore volume with 0.9% saline first, lower osmolality slowly (3 to 8 mOsm/kg/h), start low-dose insulin 0.05 units/kg/h only once glucose stops falling with fluids (earlier if ketonaemic), and give LMWH and foot protection.

sections.title: Diagnose
items: All four needed (2024 consensus): glucose 600 mg/dL (33.3 mmol/L) or more; effective osmolality (2 x Na + glucose, mmol/L) above 300 or total (plus urea) above 320 mOsm/kg; BOHB below 3.0 mmol/L or urine ketones below 2+; pH 7.3 or above and bicarbonate 15 mmol/L or above.

Typical patient: older adult with type 2 diabetes (sometimes undiagnosed), developing over days to weeks, marked dehydration (fluid loss 100 to 220 mL/kg), confusion or drowsiness, often with an acute illness.
Common precipitants: chest or urinary infection, MI, stroke, glucocorticoids, thiazides, poor fluid intake. Mortality is higher than DKA, largely from vascular events and the precipitant.
Mixed DKA/HHS (BOHB above 3.0 mmol/L with pH below 7.3 or bicarbonate below 15): treat on the DKA pathway with insulin 0.1 units/kg/h but correct osmolality slowly.

sections.title: Investigations
items: Glucose (lab and capillary), sodium, potassium, urea, creatinine, calculated osmolality (use 2 x Na + glucose until urea is available), venous gas with lactate, capillary ketones, CBC, CRP.
Blood and urine cultures, chest X-ray, ECG and troponin; CT brain if neurology is focal or does not improve with treatment.
Corrected sodium: an initial rise in sodium as glucose falls is expected (about 1.6 mmol/L per 100 mg/dL fall in glucose) and is not by itself a reason to give hypotonic fluid.

sections.title: First 6 hours: fluids first
items: 0.9% saline 1 L IV over the first hour (faster if systolic BP below 90 mmHg), then 0.5 to 1 L/h guided by clinical state. Aim for a positive balance of 2 to 3 L by 6 hours.
Do NOT start insulin at once unless ketotic. Glucose falls with fluid alone; early insulin can cause circulatory collapse and too rapid an osmolar shift.

Start fixed-rate IV insulin 0.05 units/kg/h once glucose has stopped falling on adequate fluids. Start it immediately if BOHB is above 1.0 but not above 3.0 mmol/L without acidosis (0.05 units/kg/h), or if there is mixed DKA/HHS (0.1 units/kg/h).
Potassium in fluids (JBDS): K above 5.5 mmol/L none; K 3.5 to 5.5 mmol/L add 40 mmol/L; K below 3.5 mmol/L needs senior review for additional potassium.
Measure glucose, sodium, potassium, urea and calculated osmolality hourly for the first 6 hours, then 2-hourly if the response is satisfactory.
Give prophylactic LMWH for the whole admission unless contraindicated. Protect heels and check feet daily (assume high risk if obtunded).

sections.title: Targets and fluid adjustment (6 to 24 hours)
items: Osmolality should fall 3.0 to 8.0 mOsm/kg/h. Glucose fall should not exceed 90 mg/dL/h (5 mmol/L/h). Sodium should fall no more than 10 mmol/L in 24 hours.

Osmolality falling faster than 8 mOsm/kg/h: slow the fluids and/or insulin. Glucose not falling: check fluid balance and increase saline if the positive balance is inadequate; if balance is adequate, start insulin 0.05 units/kg/h or, if already running, increase to 0.1 units/kg/h.
Switch to 0.45% saline (same rate) only if osmolality is rising or not falling despite an adequate positive fluid balance.

Keep glucose 180 to 270 mg/dL (10 to 15 mmol/L) in the first 24 hours (JBDS). Once glucose is below 250 mg/dL (14 mmol/L), add 5% or 10% glucose at 125 mL/h and continue insulin and the saline; HHS resolution includes glucose below 250 mg/dL (2024 consensus).
Aim for a positive balance of 3 to 6 L by 12 hours and replace the remaining estimated loss over the next 12 hours. Full biochemical normalisation may take up to 72 hours.

sections.title: Monitoring and resolution
items: Hourly capillary glucose and fluid balance (urine output at least 0.5 mL/kg/h); sodium and osmolality 2-hourly from 6 to 12 hours, then 4-hourly if improving; check ketones until resolution.
Reassess conscious level every 1 to 2 hours: deterioration suggests cerebral oedema, osmotic demyelination, fluid overload or a new event (stroke, sepsis).
Resolution: osmolality below 300 mOsm/kg, urine output above 0.5 mL/kg/h, cognition back to baseline and glucose below 250 mg/dL (13.9 mmol/L).
Then convert to SC insulin when eating (give SC basal 1 to 2 hours before stopping the infusion). Many can later return to oral agents after a period of stability.

sections.title: HDU or ICU referral (JBDS)
items: Osmolality above 350 mOsm/kg, sodium above 160 mmol/L, pH below 7.1, K below 3.5 or above 6.0 mmol/L on admission, GCS below 12.

SpO2 below 92% on air, systolic BP below 90 mmHg, pulse above 100 or below 60 per minute, urine output below 0.5 mL/kg/h, creatinine above 200 micromol/L (2.3 mg/dL) or AKI, hypothermia, MI or stroke.
If the patient is not improving at any stage, seek senior and diabetes team advice.

sections.title: Older adults and comorbidity
items: Older adults, heart failure or CKD: use smaller boluses (for example 250 mL) with frequent reassessment; too fast risks pulmonary oedema, too slow fails to reverse AKI.
ESKD on dialysis: expect higher glucose and osmolality, hyponatraemia and hyperkalaemia with fluid overload risk; give fluid and potassium cautiously and involve the renal team.
Patients under 18 managed by paediatric teams need a paediatric HHS protocol.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Starting insulin at DKA doses before fluids in pure HHS.
Switching to hypotonic fluid because sodium rises early, when osmolality is actually falling appropriately.
Omitting VTE prophylaxis: HHS is strongly prothrombotic.
Missing heel pressure ulcers in obtunded patients.

drugs.name: 0.9% sodium chloride
drugs.dose: 1 L IV over the first hour, then 0.5 to 1 L/h; target positive balance 2 to 3 L by 6 hours and 3 to 6 L by 12 hours
drugs.notes: 0.45% saline only if osmolality is not falling despite adequate positive balance.

drugs.name: Regular (soluble) insulin, IV fixed-rate infusion
drugs.dose: 0.05 units/kg/h IV once glucose stops falling with fluids; 0.1 units/kg/h for mixed DKA/HHS
drugs.notes: Start at once if BOHB above 1.0 mmol/L. Increase to 0.1 units/kg/h if glucose not falling despite adequate fluids.

drugs.name: Potassium chloride
drugs.dose: 40 mmol per litre of fluid when K is 3.5 to 5.5 mmol/L; none if above 5.5 mmol/L
drugs.notes: K below 3.5 mmol/L: senior review, more potassium needed, cardiac monitoring.

drugs.name: Glucose 5% or 10%
drugs.dose: 125 mL/h IV when glucose falls below 250 mg/dL (14 mmol/L), alongside 0.9% saline
drugs.notes: Target glucose 180 to 270 mg/dL (10 to 15 mmol/L) in the first 24 hours.

drugs.name: Enoxaparin (LMWH prophylaxis)
drugs.dose: 40 mg SC once daily for the whole admission
drugs.notes: Reduce dose if creatinine clearance is below 30 mL/min. Consider extended prophylaxis if very high risk.
